Which of these four is a physicist?
Who among these is a chemist?
Stephanie Kwolek is a chemist. Stephanie Louise Kwolek (July 31, 1923 – June 18, 2014) was a Polish-American chemist known for inventing Kevlar (poly-paraphenylene terephthalamide).
What is the atomic number of Tennessine?
Tennessine is a synthetic element; it has symbol Ts and atomic number 117.
What is the atomic number of Astatine?
Astatine is a chemical element; it has symbol At and atomic number 85.
In what year did Tomitaro Makino die?
Tomitaro Makino (牧野 富太郎, Makino Tomitarō; 24 April 1862 – 18 January 1957) was a pioneer Japanese botanist noted for his taxonomic work.
In what year was Aluminium discovered?
Aluminium (the Commonwealth and preferred IUPAC name) or aluminum (North American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Al and atomic number 13.
Which company manufactures Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird?
Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird: Skunk Works. The SR-71 was developed in the 1960s as a black project by Lockheed's Skunk Works division.
Cro-Magnon: France. Cro-Magnons produced Upper Palaeolithic cultures, the first major one being the Aurignacian, which was succeeded by the Gravettian by 30,000 years ago.
Who is credited with discovering Tucana?
Tucana: Petrus Plancius. Tucana (The Toucan) is a constellation in the southern sky, named after the toucan, a South American bird.
Who is credited with discovering Cro-Magnon?
Cro-Magnon: Louis Lartet. Cro-Magnons produced Upper Palaeolithic cultures, the first major one being the Aurignacian, which was succeeded by the Gravettian by 30,000 years ago.
Who is credited with discovering Makemake?
Makemake: Michael E. Brown. Makemake (minor-planet number 136472) is a dwarf planet orbiting the Sun in the Kuiper belt, a disc of icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, this family of hook-billed raptors includes buzzards, vultures, and kites across 75 genera — which family is this?
Accipitridae is one of the four families within the order Accipitriformes, and is a family of small to large birds of prey with strongly hooked bills and variable morphology based on diet.
A close relative of the peach in the genus Prunus, this drupe's seed isn't a true nut and can be "blanched" by softening its skin in hot water before peeling — what is it?
This British-American theoretical physicist at the University of Illinois reshaped our understanding of superfluid helium, work crowned by the 2003 Nobel Prize in Physics — who was he?
Anthony Leggett (26 March 1938 - 8 March 2026) was a British-American theoretical physicist and professor at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC).
This common long-term inflammatory airway disease causes wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath that can flare into sudden attacks triggered by allergens or pollen. What condition is it?
Asthma is a common long-term inflammatory disease of the airways. It is characterized by variable and recurring symptoms and reduced lung function.
Strawberries, blackcurrants and blueberries all count in the kitchen sense — though botanists would object, since the culinary meaning of this word differs from the scientific one. What word?
Berry is a small, pulpy, and often edible fruit.

Developed in Germany from the Old English Bulldog and the now-extinct Bullenbeisser, this medium-to-large mastiff-type dog breed is known for its square muzzle, underbite, and powerful bite — name the breed?
Boxer (dog breed) is a medium to large, short-haired dog breed of mastiff-type, developed in Germany.
The leaves and buds of this evergreen shrub, when processed differently, yield green, black, oolong, white, and yellow varieties of the world's most popular hot beverage — what's the species?
Camellia sinensis is a species of evergreen shrub or small tree in the flowering plant family Theaceae.
In calculus, this formula lets you find the derivative of a composed function h(x) = z(y(x)) using the derivatives of z and y separately — what is it called?
Chain rule is a formula that expresses the derivative of the composition of two differentiable functions z and y in terms of the derivatives of z and y.
Living in a symbiotic partnership with sea anemones that shelter them from predators, these Indo-Pacific reef fish live in groups led by a dominant breeding female. What fish are they?
Clownfish (genus Amphiprion) are saltwater fish found in the warm and tropical waters of the Indo-Pacific.
Which genus of passerine birds, whose Latin name literally means 'raven,' includes about 46 species commonly known as crows, ravens, and rooks?
Corvus is a widely distributed genus of passerine birds ranging from medium-sized to large-sized in the family Corvidae.
Used to treat ADHD and narcolepsy, this 'right-handed' mirror-image form of a stimulant molecule is also misused to boost cognitive and athletic performance — what is it?
Dextroamphetamine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant and enantiomer of amphetamine that is used in the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and narcolepsy.
Long used in traditional Indigenous medicine, this prairie-dwelling genus of purple daisy relatives gets its name from a Greek word meaning 'hedgehog' — what plant is it?
Echinacea is a genus of herbaceous flowering plants in the daisy family.

Discovered in January 2005 by a Palomar Observatory team and named after a Greco-Roman goddess of strife, this trans-Neptunian object is the most massive known dwarf planet in the solar system — which one?
Eris (dwarf planet) (minor-planet number 136199) is the most massive and second-largest known dwarf planet in the Solar System.
With over two hundred species across fifty genera, this bird family includes canaries, siskins, redpolls, grosbeaks, and the Hawaiian honeycreepers — which family of seed-eating passerines?
Finch are small to medium-sized passerine birds in the family Fringillidae.
Caused by abnormalities in the genome, this category of health problem may arise from a single faulty gene, many genes, or a chromosome abnormality — what is the general term?
Genetic disorder is a health problem caused by one or more abnormalities in the genome.
Nicknamed the 'benevolent dictator for life' of the language he invented, this Dutch programmer relinquished that title in July 2018. Who is he?
Guido van Rossum (born 31 January 1956) is a Dutch programmer.
This genus of the mallow family includes several hundred species prized for their large, showy blooms, and is sometimes known by the alternate name rose mallow — name the genus?
Hibiscus is a genus of common flowering plants in the mallow family, Malvaceae.
Prized in folk medicine as an antiseptic and expectorant, this Lamiaceae shrub grows wild from Southern Europe to the Caspian Sea area — which plant is it?
Hyssopus officinalis is a shrub in the Lamiaceae or mint family native to Southern Europe, the Middle East, and the region surrounding the Caspian Sea.
This Canadian-American physical educator invented an entire sport, wrote its original rule book after moving to the United States, and founded the University of Kansas's program in 1898 — who is he?
James Naismith (November 6, 1861 - November 28, 1939) was a Canadian-American physical educator, physician, Christian chaplain, and sports coach, best known as the inventor of the game of basketball.
Cousin to the wallaby and wallaroo in the family Macropodidae, this Australian marsupial's biggest member is the red one. What is it?
Kangaroo are marsupials from the subfamily Macropodinae (macropods, meaning "large foot").

Which citrus-scented perennial herb in the mint family, whose genus name Melissa comes from the Greek for 'honey bee,' is naturalized worldwide after originating in the Mediterranean and Central Asia?
Lemon balm (Melissa officinalis) is a perennial herbaceous plant in the mint family.
This Berkeley professor upended classical logic by proposing 'fuzzy' mathematics — fuzzy sets, fuzzy logic, fuzzy control, and more — who was he?

Lotfi A. Zadeh (4 February 1921 - 6 September 2017) was a mathematician, computer scientist, electrical engineer, artificial intelligence researcher, and professor of computer science at the University of California, Berkeley.
Sharing the 1963 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on nuclear shell structure, this German-American theorist became only the second woman ever to win that prize, after Marie Curie — who was she?
Maria Goeppert Mayer (ne Goppert; June 28, 1906 - February 20, 1972) was a German-American theoretical physicist who shared the 1963 Nobel Prize in Physics with J. Hans D. Jensen.
This branch of economics studies how individuals and firms allocate scarce resources within individual markets, as opposed to the economy as a whole — what field is it?

Microeconomics is a branch of economics that studies the behavior of individuals and firms in making decisions regarding the allocation of scarce resources and the interactions among these individuals and firms.
This semiaquatic rodent can stay submerged for up to seventeen minutes, propelled mainly by its webbed hind feet while its long, scaly tail helps steer — what animal is it?
Muskrat (Ondatra zibethicus) is a medium-sized semiaquatic rodent.
A reddish-brown gas that's a key step in making nitric acid for fertilizer, it also seeps into homes from gas-stove cooking and harms indoor air — which compound, formula NO2?
Nitrogen dioxide is a chemical compound with the formula NO2.

This group of middle-ear inflammations includes a painful acute infection that makes young children tug at their ears, plus a quieter form defined by non-infectious fluid lingering for weeks. What is the condition?
Otitis media is a group of inflammatory diseases of the middle ear.
Built for the sea, it sports a spiny tongue and powerful jaws to grip slippery fish, then swallows them whole mid-swim. Which animal splits its life half on land, half in the water?
Penguin are a group of flightless semi-aquatic sea birds which live almost exclusively in the Southern Hemisphere.
Native to South America and the most economically important member of the Bromeliaceae family, this tropical 'multiple fruit' became a 17th-century European symbol of luxury — what is it?
Pineapple (Ananas comosus) is a tropical plant with an edible fruit; it is the most economically significant plant in the family Bromeliaceae.

This male sexual dysfunction occurs when orgasm happens very soon after minimal sexual stimulation, with medical experts generally setting the threshold at around one minute — what's this condition called?

Premature ejaculation (PE) is a male sexual dysfunction that occurs when a male expels semen (and most likely experiences orgasm) soon after beginning sexual activity, and with minimal penile stimulation.
This colorless, odorless radioactive noble gas has the atomic number 86, and its longest-lived isotope has a half-life of under four days — name the element?
Radon is a chemical element; it has symbol Rn and atomic number 86.
Known by the common name 'dog rose,' this climbing wild rose species is native across Europe and stretches into northwest Africa and western Asia — which species?
Rosa canina is a variable climbing, wild rose species native to Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia.

Seven living species make up this group of ocean-dwelling reptiles, five of which are threatened with extinction — one species, found only near Australia, Papua New Guinea, and Indonesia, is not — name this group?
Sea turtle (superfamily Chelonioidea), sometimes called marine turtles, are reptiles of the order Testudines and of the suborder Cryptodira.
Whether on land, in fresh water, or in the sea, this gastropod earns its name from a coiled shell roomy enough to fully retract into — what is it?
Snail is a shelled gastropod. The name is most often applied to land snails, terrestrial pulmonate gastropod molluscs.
This group of cartilaginous fish spans eleven families and roughly 220 species, from tiny river-dwellers to giant manta and devil rays — what group of fish is it?
Stingray are a group of rays, a type of cartilaginous fish.
This fibrous connective tissue connects muscle to bone, unlike its cousin which connects bone to bone, and numbers about 4,000 throughout the adult human body — what is it?
Tendon is a tough band of dense fibrous connective tissue that connects muscle to bone.
Caused by superantigens from staph or strep bacteria, this condition brings fever, a sunburn-like rash, and peeling skin, and has been tied to absorbent tampon use — which condition?
Toxic shock syndrome (TSS) is a condition caused by bacterial toxins.
This abnormal enlargement of the vein network draining the testicles is the most common correctable cause of male infertility, found in over a third of men with the condition. Name it?
Varicocele is an abnormal enlargement of the pampiniform venous plexus in the scrotum.
This biological process unfolds in predictable phases — hemostasis, inflammation, cell proliferation, and tissue remodeling — to replace damaged skin after the barrier is broken. What is it?
Wound healing refers to a living organism's replacement of destroyed or damaged tissue by newly produced tissue.
The simplest alkyne, this colorless gas packs all four of its atoms into one straight line thanks to a carbon-carbon triple bond, and fuels welding torches — which compound is it?
First nominated by Ronald Reagan in 1987 and reappointed every four years until 2006, this soft-spoken economist logged the second-longest tenure ever as chairman of the Federal Reserve — who was he?
Alan Greenspan: American economist and financial advisor (born 1926)

Nicknamed 'lazy eye,' this childhood vision disorder occurs when the brain favors one eye over the other, and correcting the underlying cause doesn't restore sight right away — what is this condition?
Amblyopia: Failure of the brain to process input from one eye.
Comprising over 22,000 species including ragworms, earthworms, and leeches, this phylum of segmented worms use parapodia to move — what is it?
Annelid: Phylum of segmented worms. The basic annelid form consists of multiple segments called metameres.

Known only from fragmentary remains including vertebrae and a giant femur first found by a farmer in 1987, this titanosaur may be the largest land animal ever discovered, stretching up to 35 meters — which genus?
Argentinosaurus: Late Cretaceous giant sauropod dinosaur genus.
This broad category of technology uses machines and predetermined rules to reduce the need for human intervention in factories, boilers, and telephone switching — what is it?
Automation: Use of various control systems for operating equipment.

Nicknamed 'Huey,' this American utility helicopter became the first turbine-powered rotorcraft in U.S. military service, developed in the 1950s to meet an Army need for medical evacuation and utility missions. Which aircraft?
Bell UH-1 Iroquois: Huey family of American military utility helicopters.
This medical term for blood escaping the circulatory system describes a healthy person as able to lose 10 to 15 percent of their total volume without serious harm — what is it called?
Bleeding: Blood escaping from the circulatory system. Bleeding, hemorrhage, haemorrhage or blood loss, is blood escaping from the circulatory system from damaged blood vessels.
Typically about two-thirds copper and one-third zinc, which prehistoric substitutional alloy differs from bronze, which swaps in tin instead of zinc?
Brass: Alloy of copper and zinc. Brass has long been popular for its bright, golden appearance and is used for drawer pulls and doorknobs.
This silvery-gold alkali metal has a melting point just above room temperature, making it one of only five elemental metals that go liquid in warm conditions — what is it?
Caesium: Chemical element with atomic number 55 (Cs)
This Cornell astronomer worked on the Mariner, Viking, and Voyager missions and won a Pulitzer for 'The Dragons of Eden' — who is this famed science communicator?
Carl Sagan: American scientist and science communicator (1934–1996)
Known commonly as tapeworms, this class of ribbon-like parasitic flatworms sheds egg-packed segments called proglottids — what is this class called?
Cestoda: Class of flatworms. Cestoda is a class of parasitic worms in the flatworm phylum (Platyhelminthes).
Blooming in autumn and closely associated with the month of November, this East Asian flowering genus in the daisy family boasts thousands of horticultural varieties — which flower?
Chrysanthemum: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family.

Believed to be the first coffee species ever cultivated, this plant, native to the forests of Ethiopia, South Sudan, and Yemen, still accounts for roughly 60% of global coffee production — what's its scientific name?
Coffea arabica: Species of coffee plant. Coffea arabica, also known as the Arabica coffee, is a species of flowering plant in the coffee and madder family Rubiaceae.
Produced mainly by the adrenal cortex and surging in response to stress and low blood sugar, this steroid hormone is sold as medicine under the name hydrocortisone — what is it?
Built from microfilaments, intermediate filaments, and microtubules, this network gives a cell its shape and lets it contract and migrate — what is it?
Cytoskeleton: Network of filamentous proteins that forms the internal framework of cells.
Native to the Mediterranean and nicknamed 'clove pink' for a spicy fragrance reminiscent of cinnamon and nutmeg, what flower is this?
Dianthus caryophyllus: Species of flowering plant.
Element 105 sparked a long Cold War naming dispute, claimed first by a Soviet institute in 1968 and then by Berkeley in 1970 before being settled in 1993 — which synthetic element?
Dubnium: Chemical element with atomic number 105 (Db)
The second-largest member of the deer family, this animal is also called "wapiti," a Shawnee and Cree word meaning "white rump" for the pale fur it flashes to signal alarm — what animal is it?
Elk: Species of deer. The word "elk" originally referred to the European variety of the moose, Alces alces, but was transferred to Cervus canadensis by North American colonists.

In 2019 this French-American MIT economist shared the Nobel with her husband and Michael Kremer for an experimental approach to fighting global poverty, rooted in the randomized trials of her J-PAL lab — who is she?
This front-of-the-head body part houses most sense organs — eyes, nose, and mouth — and its damage or scarring can profoundly affect a person's sense of identity. What is it?
Face: Front of a head. The face is the front of the head in humans and many other animals that features most of the sense organs including the eyes, nose and mouth.
This normal, occasionally embarrassing bodily process brings intestinal gas to the rectum, pressurizes it with muscle contractions, and releases it through the anus — what is it?
Flatulence: Bodily function of expelling intestinal gas from the anus.

After dropping out of Harvard to help build early versions of Windows at Microsoft, this developer co-founded a studio that made Half-Life and later launched a digital storefront called Steam — who is he?
Known only from teeth and four jawbones, this extinct genus of giant ape roamed China for nearly two million years and is now thought to be a close relative of the orangutan — what is it?
Gigantopithecus: Extinct genus of primate. The species may have been sexually dimorphic, with males much bigger than females.
One of the heaviest snakes alive, which non-venomous constrictor prefers shallow, slow-moving South American waters like flooded grasslands and rivers?
In music theory, this concept for combining different pitches into chords and progressions has both a 'vertical' frequency dimension and a 'horizontal' time dimension — what is it called?
Harmony: Aspect of music. In music, harmony is the concept of combining different sounds in order to create new, distinct musical ideas.

A Greek physician and philosopher of the classical era, this figure is hailed as the "Father of Medicine" for championing prognosis, clinical observation, and the now-discredited theory of bodily humors — who is he?
Hippocrates: Ancient Greek physician (c. 460 – c. 370 BCE)
Though phylogenetically closer to cats, these African carnivores resemble dogs thanks to convergent evolution, and their family has just four living species — what animal is it?
Fever, sore throat, body aches and fatigue that start one to four days after exposure and may spiral into pneumonia — there are four types of this viral infection. What is it?
Working under Tamerlane around 1400, this Persian astronomer and mathematician produced work that mostly never reached Europe and stays largely unpublished — who is it?
Jamshid al-Kashi: Persian astronomer and mathematician (c. 1380–1429)
Fluent in Quechua after being raised in two Indigenous households as a child, this Peruvian novelist and anthropologist became known for his intimate portrayals of Andean culture — who is he?
Named from a Norwegian word for 'small fry of fish,' these shrimp-like crustaceans form a biomass of some 379 million tonnes in the Southern Ocean alone — which creatures?

Krill: Small, shrimp-like crustaceans; order of crustaceans. Krill (Euphausiids) (sing.: krill) are small and exclusively marine crustaceans of the order Euphausiacea, found in all of the world's oceans.
Marked by weariness and a desire to act without the energy to do so, which condition can be a normal response to poor sleep or stress, or a sign of underlying illness?
Lethargy: State of tiredness, weariness, fatigue, or lack of energy.
Predominantly black and white with pink and grey highlights, this small Eurasian bird forms social flocks of six to seventeen outside breeding season and often nests in thorny scrub. What is it?
Long-tailed tit: Species of bird in Europe and Asia.

Discovered in 2005 by the same Palomar team whose haul of big, icy Kuiper-belt bodies pushed astronomers to demote Pluto in 2006, this fourth-largest dwarf planet has a methane-frosted, tholin-reddened surface — what is it?
Makemake: Dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt. Makemake (minor-planet number 136472) is a dwarf planet orbiting the Sun in the Kuiper belt, a disc of icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Distinguished by its darker camouflage, conformal fuel tanks, and a two-seat cockpit, this all-weather multirole fighter first flew in 1986 for long-range interdiction missions — what is it?
McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle: American all-weather multirole fighter aircraft.

Born from the French Revolution's push to standardize units into the metric system, this scientific field oversees everything from the SI unit system to the labs that keep rulers honest — what is it called?
Metrology: Science of measurement and its application.
Making up about 23% of all named marine organisms, this phylum is the second-largest in the animal kingdom after the arthropods — what is it?
This lipid-rich substance wraps around nerve axons in segments, leaving gaps called nodes of Ranvier that let electrical signals leap along in a process called saltatory conduction — what is it?
Myelin: Fatty substance insulating nerve cell axons.
This Renaissance polymath put the Sun, not Earth, at the center of the universe in a book published just before his death in 1543 — kicking off a revolution in science. Who was he?

With atomic number 118, this synthetic element boasts the highest atomic number and mass of any known element, and was named to honor the physicist who led the hunt for the periodic table's heaviest members — what is it?
Oganesson: Chemical element with atomic number 118 (Og)
Making up most of Earth's crust, this class of chemical compound pairs oxygen with another element — the same chemistry behind the thin protective layer on aluminium foil — what is it called?
Oxide: Compounds containing an oxygen atom.
Carl Linnaeus named this crop 'hypogaea' — Greek for 'under the earth' — because, unlike most legumes, it ripens its pods below ground. What is it?
Peanut: Legume cultivated as a grain and oil crop.
Grouped within the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae, this genus contains today's living flamingo species — which genus?
This inflammatory lung condition attacks the tiny air sacs called alveoli, usually after a viral or bacterial infection, and often shows up on a chest X-ray — what is it?
Pneumonia: Inflammation of the alveoli of the lungs.
Manufactured in a soybean-oil emulsion that gives it a milky white look, this IV anesthetic — sold as Diprivan — induces unconsciousness fast and lets patients wake quickly; what is it?
Propofol: Intravenous medication used in anesthesia.
Guided by empiricist and positivist philosophy, which academic methodology turns data collection into numbers to test theories across the natural, applied, formal, and social sciences?
Quantitative research: All procedures for the numerical representation of empirical facts.
Native to South and Southeast Asia, this non-venomous constrictor is the world's longest snake and has been spotted swimming far out at sea — what species is it?
Reticulated python: Species of snake. It is the world's longest snake, and the third heaviest after the green anaconda and Burmese python.
Discovered in 1973 by Ruth Bishop via electron micrograph images, this fecal-oral pathogen is the leading cause of diarrheal illness in infants worldwide — which pathogen?
Rotavirus: Specific genus of RNA viruses.

Discovered in 1879 via spectral analysis of Scandinavian minerals, this silvery-white rare-earth element with atomic number 21 wasn't isolated in metallic form until 1937, and today it's prized for strengthening aluminum alloys — which element?
Scandium: Chemical element with atomic number 21 (Sc)
An adult female of this ruminant is a ewe, a castrated male a wether, and a young one a lamb — and with about 1.2 billion of them, they're easily the most common of their kind. What animal?
Sheep: Domesticated ruminant bred for meat, wool, and milk.
Nicknamed a 'truth serum' in popular culture despite dubious real-world reliability, this fast-acting barbiturate anesthetic is marketed under the brand name Pentothal — which drug?
Sodium thiopental: Barbiturate general anesthetic. It is the thiobarbiturate analog of pentobarbital, and an analog of thiobarbital.

An English dyer and astronomer, he was the first to systematically show, around 1729, that electricity could travel through metals — flipping the era's focus from mere static sparks to conduction. Who was he?
Stephen Gray (scientist): English physicist. Stephen Gray (December 1666 – February 1736) was an English dyer and astronomer who was the first to systematically experiment with electrical conduction.
Commonly known as fainting, this fast-onset, short-duration loss of consciousness and muscle strength is typically caused by a sudden drop in blood flow to the brain — what's the medical term?
Syncope (medicine): Transient loss of consciousness and postural tone.
Also sold under the name dronabinol, this principal psychoactive compound in cannabis is prescribed to relieve chemotherapy-induced nausea and HIV/AIDS-related appetite loss — what is it?
Tetrahydrocannabinol: Psychoactive component of cannabis. It is the principal psychoactive constituent of Cannabis and one of at least 113 total cannabinoids identified on the plant.
Sitting between cells and organs in the body's organization, this assembly of similar cells and their extracellular matrix takes its English name from a French word meaning 'to weave' — what is it?
Tissue (biology): Group of similar cells performing a specific function.
Roughly three times stiffer than steel and nearly as hard as diamond, this gray powder is sintered into cutting tools, armor-piercing bullets, and jewelry — what compound is it?
Tungsten carbide: Hard, dense and stiff chemical compound.
Unlike arteries, most of these thin-walled blood vessels carry deoxygenated blood back toward the heart — what are they?
Vein: Blood vessels that carry blood towards the heart.
A slow-moving filter-feeder and the largest known fish alive — the biggest reliably recorded stretched nearly 19 metres — this is the only living member of its family. What is it?
Whale shark: Largest living species of fish. The whale shark (Rhincodon typus) is a slow-moving, filter-feeding carpet shark and the largest known extant fish species.
These striped African equines share their genus with horses and asses, and the leading theory says their patterns evolved mainly to deter biting flies — what are they?
Zebra: Striped animal in the equid family.
What is the chemical symbol for bohrium?
The symbol for bohrium is Bh. Bohrium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bh and atomic number 107.
The symbol for neon is Ne. Neon is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ne and the atomic number 10.

Paul Newman: Paul Leonard Newman (January 26, 1925 – September 26, 2008) was an American actor, filmmaker, racecar driver, philanthropist, and entrepreneur.

Rebecca Ferguson: Rebecca Louisa Ferguson Sundström (Swedish: [rɛˈbɛ̂kːa lʊˈîːsa ˈfæ̂rɡɵˌsɔn ˈsɵ̂nːstrœm]; born 19 October 1983) is a Swedish actress.

In what year was A Good Person first released?
